rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that a reply to a sent request either carries the decision information directly or announces that the decision will be delayed, and the process continues differently depending on which of these the reply contains: Model one receiving step for the reply, followed directly by an exclusive gateway. Give the gateway one outgoing branch per content condition, with each condition taken from the description's wording (for example, decision information present versus delay announced). Do not model the choice as an event-based gateway with a separate catch event for each possible reply. Place any follow-up step the description ties to one content condition on that condition's branch only.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that a reply to a sent request either carries the decision information directly or announces that the decision will be delayed, and the process continues differently depending on which of these the reply contains

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says that a reply from an external party can announce a delay before the final result, and that the process then presents a message to the user before the final result is expected: Model the event that receives the delay announcement as an intermediate catch event, followed directly by a task that presents the delay message to the user. Route the flow from that task to the event that receives the final result, so that the user notice is performed before the process waits again. Do not connect the delay event directly to the final-result wait when a stated user-facing action lies between them.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says that a reply from an external party can announce a delay before the final result, and that the process then presents a message to the user before the final result is expected

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says a user-facing interface, distinct from the back-end process, is operated by a person who is not part of the process owner, starts the back-end process with a request, and afterwards gets back its outcome or notices from that process: Model the user-facing interface as its own bpmn:participant pool in the same collaboration as the back-end process. Add a message flow from the interface pool to the start event that the request triggers. For each outcome or notice the description says the back-end sends back to the interface, add a message flow from the sending task in the back-end pool to the interface pool. Keep the back-end's internal steps inside its own pool, and do not model the interface's receipt as a task or event inside the back-end pool.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says a user-facing interface, distinct from the back-end process, is operated by a person who is not part of the process owner, starts the back-end process with a request, and afterwards gets back its outcome or notices from that process

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says a process receives a reply from an outside party and then presents its content to a human user, who acts on it before the process continues: Model the receipt of the reply as one receiving step on the branch for the content it carries. Then model the presentation to the user as a task that performs that work, placed directly after the receipt and before any later wait or the end of the process. Do not connect a branch straight from the receipt to a later wait or to the end when the description has a presentation step on that branch. Model the receipt as a catch event only when the description names a message, signal, time, or condition that the process waits for.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says a process receives a reply from an outside party and then presents its content to a human user, who acts on it before the process continues

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description names an outside party that acts on its own and exchanges messages with the process, such as sending the process a notice or result it waits for, or receiving an outcome the process sends back, and the generated model connects a sending task to a catch event inside the same process pool: Model the outside party as its own black-box pool in the same collaboration. Draw every message exchange with that party as a message flow between the two pools: a message flow from the party's pool to the process's receiving element (start event or intermediate catch event), and a message flow from the process's sending task to the party's pool. Do not connect a sending task to a catch event inside the same pool with a message flow, and do not use a sequence flow for the exchange.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description names an outside party that acts on its own and exchanges messages with the process, such as sending the process a notice or result it waits for, or receiving an outcome the process sends back, and the generated model connects a sending task to a catch event inside the same process pool

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says a process sends a request to an external party and the reply is either an immediate outcome or a delay status that is followed by a later outcome, so the process must branch on which kind of reply arrives: Model the request as a send task in the process pool. Place an exclusive gateway after it that routes on the kind of reply received: one branch for an immediate outcome and one for the delay path. On the delay path, model the external party's delay report and its later outcome as send tasks in that party's pool, in the order the description gives, linked to the process by message flows. Do not replace this decision with an event-based gateway, because the description states a condition on the reply, not a race between events.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says a process sends a request to an external party and the reply is either an immediate outcome or a delay status that is followed by a later outcome, so the process must branch on which kind of reply arrives
